title: Smuggling of 1.5M AI GPUs could be the cause of Huang's departure
lede: Tom's Hardware covers a SemiAnalysis estimate that over 1.5 GW of export-restricted Nvidia hardware reached China, and its theory that this, not only Huang's personal life, explains his exit.

points: SemiAnalysis's accelerator tracking puts restricted Nvidia shipments to China above 1.5 GW, roughly 1.5 to 2.1 million GPUs depending on the H200 and B200 mix.
Parts built for China's rules, such as the H20 and H800, are excluded from the figure.
It points to the Supermicro case, where $510 million of servers allegedly went to China, and a Taiwan case in which 74 B300 servers reached China.
Analysts speculate some in US intelligence wanted Huang out over his opposition to tighter controls, but offer no direct evidence.
SemiAnalysis favours letting Chinese firms rent overseas compute under US oversight rather than a total ban.

points.text: Many say a CEO's affairs are private until they touch espionage or illegal exports, at which point they become public business.
Commenters with clearance experience say affairs matter less morally than as leverage a rival state could use.
Some doubt the motive: a reply notes the sums involved are small for a billionaire, so greed alone seems an unlikely explanation.
A thread splits over claims that idle data-centre GPUs will flow to China, with a reply citing B200 spot prices up 64% in three months.
